answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards face-down; return the others unseen. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories; randomly select one structure bonus tile and place face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards; structure bonus tile; 11 marked territories; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: Place character at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs on Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six technology cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat; leave one-time recruit spaces empty. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup pieces table and steps 3–4.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Normally a section cannot repeat from the previous turn; Rusviet may repeat it. If taking both, top must precede bottom. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full first, then choose any amount of exposed green-box benefits; exact bottom costs and coins vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section; optional actions; full cost then optional benefits.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities, though your Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay resource costs with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases section.

answers.answer: Normal Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker can later move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its subsequent move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins; all units can carry resources; only mechs carry your workers; carried movement does not count as own movement.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech may enter, then must stop and cannot move again that turn; the enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Retreat still happens if you lack popularity. Your own workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control that territory.
answers.evidence: Enemy workers only; Speed stop rules.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses order among multiple combats. Workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs; your character/mech may enter but then stops for the turn.
answers.evidence: Enemy character/mechs movement paragraph; Combat section.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and yields two power OR one combat card, before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and yields any two resources (same or different) OR one popularity, before upgrades. Place traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all your workers are home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade paragraphs.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production; then select up to two different controlled territories, and each worker there can produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come left to right from the Player Mat and go in the producing village. Benefits, including production, may be declined partly or entirely. New workers expose costs only for future Produce actions; they do not change the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce numbered sequence; new workers and future costs.

answers.answer: Upgrade pays the exposed oil cost; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box (not solid-black-bordered), improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy pays exposed metal cost; put a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its ability applies to character and every mech, not workers. Even after all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits are complete, you may pay for the bottom action to get its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions; Upgrade and Deploy entries; completed bottom action sentence.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; at most one structure total per territory, including opponents' structures. Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. Mill gives a bonus Produce territory and production while controlled, but cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Mine is your personal movement tunnel even when enemy-controlled. Enemy units do not gain your structures' abilities.
answers.evidence: Build entry; structure abilities; control section.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and permanently place it on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards, according to the space. Its ongoing bonus is the circle exposed where it was removed. For the rest of the game, you may gain that bonus when you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes that matching bottom action; active player resolves first, then left, then right, stopping at game end. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly and simultaneously selects dial power from zero up to the lesser of seven and current power, and may play up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with a zero dial; Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present, but workers alone never fight. Reveal simultaneously and total dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender; abilities resolve before combat. Both pay: selected dial power comes off the Power Track and all played cards are discarded face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
answers.evidence: Combat section: secret choices, ability order, totals, tie, and payment. (The question's phrase 'how do combat abilities resolve' is addressed by attacker-then-defender ordering and the faction abilities.)

answers.answer: Winner controls the territory and its resources. Loser sends all characters, mechs and workers to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers to an adjacent lake. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie exception. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat stars places one, while one already at two places none; Saxony places one after each victory while stars remain. A loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power on dial or through cards; zero total yields no card.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains there; this is before a following bottom action. If it loses contested entry, character retreats and encounter token remains. Gains (resources, workers, mechs, structures) go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter's printed cost only: no additional normal action cost, mat benefit, or ongoing recruit bonus applies.
answers.evidence: Encounters section.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), must look at available Factory cards, choose one, and return the rest; it is not limited to the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a Speed character/mech, within that action.
answers.evidence: Factory section.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. Meet all its requirements at reveal; place its star and put both objective cards on the deck bottom. Normally only one objective star; Saxony keeps the other card after the first and may score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section; Stars section.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Stars are permanent and cannot be lost; other players' stars do not block your achievement. Sixth star ends the game immediately, with no further turns/actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. For a neighbor recruit star, finish active action, then active player, left neighbor, right neighbor; check for sixth star at each step and stop if game ends. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement by returning initiating units to their original territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: bottom-row sequence; neighbor sequence; pending battle.

answers.answer: At popularity 10 use the 7–12 tier: five stars score $20 ($4 each); four ordinary territories plus Factory count as 7 scoring territories and score $21 ($3 each); 13 resources make six complete pairs and score $12 ($2 each). Add these to held coins and the selected structure bonus. Structures qualify for that bonus even when enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers after coins: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune tables and structure bonus eligibility; tiebreaker paragraph.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Expansion bases without matching core factions are inactive placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases section.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers, one matching token per worker in a selected producing territory. Lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource supply has no limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources paragraph.

answers.answer: Any unit can pick up, carry and drop any number of resources; a mech can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Mechs carry your workers, never your character. Speed gives each selected character/mech one extra territory, not workers; a tunnel jump still costs one step and the extra step may be before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins; Speed paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory with only an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit type.
answers.evidence: Enemy structure only; printed tunnel territories paragraph.

answers.answer: Do not pay a partial Produce cost. If you cannot afford any action, take a dead turn: move your token to a different section and take neither action. The prior Move section restriction means choose another section.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: never pay part of a cost; dead turn by moving token to a different section and taking neither action.

answers.answer: Built Armory grants one power on Trade; built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These are matching future actions (benefits are noted as available from built structures), and opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities; enemy occupation does not remove your structure benefits. Mill alone is specifically limited to producing while you control its territory.
answers.evidence: Trade/Bolster; Build abilities; control section.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is for character/mechs: Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Polania to villages and mountains; Saxony to forests and mountains. Nordic has no character/mech Riverwalk destinations: its Swim lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes, and does not help its character/mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction abilities table.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts apply to characters and mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery differs by letting you pay one power before combat to reduce opponent's power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Underpass/Disarm; Nordic Artillery entries.

answers.answer: With two mechs and three workers, Rusviet People's Army allows three combat cards total (one per participating character/mech plus one additional card when at least one worker is present). Workers alone never fight; combat requires a character or mech.
answers.evidence: People's Army; Combat steps 1–2.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It does not permit entry to an active opponent home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare entry; home-base restriction.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion, once per turn, lets you spend one combat card as any one resource regardless of its printed value.
answers.evidence: Crimea starting ability and Scout entries.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but it grants no adjacent-lake retreat. When a carrier leaves a lake, workers on lakes require a mech to move off and you cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on a lake.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy; Polania Submerge; lake carrier paragraph.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not cover popularity loss for driving out undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie entry.

answers.answer: Polania Meander may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain can pay the second cost. You must pay the printed cost of each chosen option and may take as little of its benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Meander ability; Encounters section.

answers.answer: Yes, reaching the encounter during Factory Move stops the character and it cannot move again that turn. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Encounters section explicitly says rules also apply during Factory Move.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, though you need not reveal their exact total when asked. Combat-card hand count is public; during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal, and card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until revealing a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; informal agreements are unenforceable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). A payment or negotiation cannot cancel combat after movement has initiated it; combat must be fought, though bribes may influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per counted territory, $1 per resource pair. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Each complete pair of controlled resources scores, with an odd leftover ignored.
answers.evidence: Final fortune tables and text.

answers.answer: Count each unique adjacent printed tunnel, lake, or printed encounter location across all your structures; removed encounter tokens still count. Mines are not printed tunnels. Rivers do not break adjacency. Payout for tunnels: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9; lakes: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9; encounters: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Zero qualifying features scores zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table; adjacency tile note.

answers.answer: Structures-on-tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures-in-a-row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures-on-farms/tundras combines qualifying structures on those terrain types: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6.

answers.answer: A placed popularity star is permanent, but it does not protect current popularity or its scoring tier; current popularity determines final scoring. Another player's stars never block an achievement, so two factions may each earn a star for the same achievement goal.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania clockwise, omitting inactive factions. Recruit ongoing bonuses trigger for the active player and immediate left and right neighbors, so faction order determines who is adjacent and can trigger them.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2 and ongoing recruits paragraph.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with a lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Movement terrain paragraph.

answers.answer: No. Show the drawn encounter card to all players, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud; you need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card/artwork and read capitalized thematic text.

answers.answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player is still deciding which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next player may begin after noninteractive bottom-row action starts.

answers.answer: No. A chosen top action and bottom action are each limited to once within a turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's exception only waives the previous-turn section restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: top and bottom each limited once within turn, including Rusviet.

answers.answer: The normal unupgraded Move action can instead gain $1 when you choose not to move units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. Workers forced to retreat go to the home base, not the mat, so they cannot be returned to cover a Produce cost again.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to Player Mat; enemy workers retreat to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.
answers.evidence: Combat: you may attack with zero power/popularity.

answers.answer: Yes. A non-Saxony faction with two combat stars places no more combat stars, but may still fight after reaching its combat-star limit.
answers.evidence: Combat-star award and explicit permission to keep fighting.

answers.answer: Without Meander, you must choose one affordable encounter option; you cannot decline all choices or choose an unaffordable option. You may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: must choose one affordable option; may take as little benefit as desired.

answers.answer: Combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, not in turn order. Reveal dials and selected combat cards simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1 and 3.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action to other players so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as you achieve a star goal; it cannot be declined or delayed to avoid game end. An objective is different: even when completed, you may wait to reveal it, and it earns a star only when revealed on your own turn while all requirements are still met.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved; Objectives: may wait to reveal, requirements at reveal.

answers.answer: No. By default units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Movement terrain paragraph.

answers.answer: No. The recruit token is permanently placed on the Faction Mat one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist entry.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve it or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter.

answers.answer: A controlled Mill adds one bonus producing territory to the number selected: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded three become up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker; each actual worker there may also produce normally. It can produce without an actual worker, using the territory's terrain output, while the Mill territory is controlled.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill paragraph.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not preserve control after your last unit leaves when there is no structure.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: control definition; resources stay on board.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: Bottom resources—Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.
